 __

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under Fundamental Duties?

options.text: To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
To value and preserve rich heritage

questions.solution:

__
 
• Fundamental Duties, as mentioned in **Article 51A of the Indian Constitution**, do not include securing a living wage.
 
• Instead, securing a living wage is a **Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP)** under **Article 43**, which directs the state to ensure a decent standard of life for workers.
 
• Fundamental Duties include safeguarding public property, cherishing national struggle ideals, and valuing rich heritage,
 
• These are **Introduced by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.**
 
• These duties are not **enforceable by law. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The fundamental duties can be used by the courts to determine whether a law is constitutional.
 
• The Constitution of the former USSR served as inspiration for the Indian Constitution's Fundamental Duties.
 
• One of the most significant constitutional amendments to India was the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• The Indian National Congress, led at the time by Indira Gandhi, passed it.
 
• The Indian Constitution has undergone numerous revisions as a result of this act, which is why it is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution."

• **The Gateway of India was built in the traditional Indo-Saracenic style to welcome King George V and Queen Mary to India in 1911**__. 

 __
 
• The **structure is an arch made of basalt, 26 meters** (85 feet) high.
 
• The final design of **George Wittet was sanctioned in 1914** and the construction of the monument was completed in 1924.
 
• The Gateway was later used as a symbolic ceremonial entrance to India for the Viceroys and the new Governors of Bombay.

• This style of architecture was the combination of native Indo-Islamic architecture with the Gothic revival style of Victorian Britain.
 
• The buildings built in India by Indo- Saracenic style of architecture were built according to advanced British structural engineering standards of the 1800s including infrastructures of iron, steel and poured concrete.
 
• These types of buildings were employed with domes, pointed arch, vaulted roofs, pinnacles, minarets, pierced open arcade and open pavilions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about membership in the World Trade Organization (WTO)?

options.text: It negotiates only bilateral trade agreements between countries.
All the countries of the world are members of WTO.
India reduced trade restrictions due to obligations to WTO.
It was established as a new organisation in 1991.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India reduced trade restrictions due to obligations to WTO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established on January 1, 1995.
 
• It was created as a successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which was established in 1948.
 
• The WTO deals with the global rules of trade between nations with a goal to ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible.
 
• The organization officially commenced on January 1, 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, signed by 123 nations in 1994.
 
• It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and its current Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The WTO provides a forum for negotiating agreements aimed at reducing obstacles to international trade and ensuring a level playing field for all, thus contributing to economic growth and development.
 
• It also provides a legal and institutional framework for the implementation and monitoring of these agreements, as well as for dispute resolution among countries over trade-related issues.
 
• As of the latest data, the WTO has 164 member countries, representing over 98% of global trade.
 
• One of the key functions of the WTO is to oversee the implementation, administration, and operation of the covered agreements and to provide a forum for further negotiations and monitoring of member countries' trade policies.

questions.question: At independence, which was the major employment-producing sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of India's independence in 1947, the agricultural sector was the major employment-producing sector. This sector was the backbone of the Indian economy, employing a vast majority of the population. 
 
• **Agriculture:** Agriculture was the primary source of livelihood for approximately 70-75% of the Indian population. This highlights the agrarian nature of the economy at that time. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limited Industrialization:**

 
 
• The industrial sector was relatively underdeveloped, employing only about 10% of the workforce. This was partly due to the colonial policies that had hindered the growth of indigenous industries. 
 
 
 
• **Growing Service Sector: **
 
 
• The service sector, though growing, was still limited in its capacity to absorb a large portion of the workforce, employing around 15-20%.
 
 
 
• **Rural Economy:**
 
 
• The Indian economy was predominantly rural, with most of the population residing in villages and dependent on agriculture for their sustenance.
 
 
 
• **Subsistence Farming: **
 
 
• A significant portion of agriculture was characterized by subsistence farming, where farmers primarily produced for their own consumption with limited surplus for trade. 
 
 
 
• **Traditional Practices:** 
 
 
• Agricultural practices were largely traditional, with limited use of modern technologies and inputs, resulting in low productivity.
 
 
 
• **Land Ownership:**
 
 
• Land ownership was concentrated in the hands of a few, with many farmers being landless laborers or tenants. 
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Dependence: **
 
 
• Agriculture was heavily dependent on the monsoon rains, making it vulnerable to droughts and other natural calamities. 
 
 
 
• **Stagnation: **
 
 
• The agricultural sector had experienced stagnation and even decline during the British colonial rule, due to exploitative policies and lack of investment. 
 
 
 
• **Poverty and Inequality:**
 
 
• **​ **The dominance of agriculture, coupled with its stagnation, contributed to widespread poverty and inequality in rural areas.

questions.question: What is the study of coins called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Numismatics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Numismatics:**

 
 
• The study or collection of coins, tokens, paper money, and medals.
 
• Numismatics provides insights into history, economics, and art through the study of currency.
 
• It encompasses the physical attributes of money, its production, circulation, and historical context.
 
• Numismatics includes areas like notaphily (study of paper money) and exonumia (study of tokens and medals).
 
• Numerous numismatic societies exist worldwide, such as the American Numismatic Society and the Royal Numismatic Society.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Almanac:**

 
 
• An annual publication containing a calendar, astronomical data, and other statistical information.
 
• Almanacs often include weather forecasts, tide tables, sunrise and sunset times, and historical events.
 
• They serve as a comprehensive reference source for a wide range of information.
 
• Famous almanacs include "The Old Farmer's Almanac" and "Whitaker's Almanac."
 
• Many almanacs are now available online, offering interactive features and updated data.
 
 
 
• **Petroglyphs:**
 
 
• Rock carvings or engravings made by prehistoric people.
 
• Petroglyphs are created by removing the dark outer layer of rock to expose the lighter rock underneath.
 
• They are found in various parts of the world, often in caves or on rock faces.
 
• Petroglyphs provide insights into the beliefs, practices, and daily life of ancient cultures.
 
• Notable petroglyph sites include the Three Rivers Petroglyph Site in New Mexico and the Val Camonica in Italy.
 
 
 
• **Curator:**
 
 
• A person responsible for the care and management of a museum's or gallery's collections.
 
• Curators research, acquire, preserve, and exhibit artifacts or artworks.
 
• They possess specialized knowledge in their field, such as art history or archaeology.
 
• Curators typically hold advanced degrees in their area of expertise.
 
• They play a vital role in preserving cultural heritage and making it accessible to the public.

questions.question: Who is the only living representative of the extremely ancient and diverse group, Sphenopsida, commonly known as ‘horsetails’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equisetum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equisetum (Horsetails):**

 
 
• Ancient Lineage: Equisetum represents one of the oldest surviving genera of plants, with fossil records dating back over 300 million years to the Carboniferous period. They are considered "living fossils".
 
• Sphenopsida Class: They belong to the class Sphenopsida, a group of plants that were much more diverse and prominent in the past.
 
• Hollow Stems: Equisetum species have distinctive hollow, jointed stems that are often ribbed.
 
• Silica Content: Their cell walls are heavily impregnated with silica, giving them a rough texture and making them useful for scouring.
 
• Reproduction: They reproduce by spores, not seeds, and have underground rhizomes for vegetative spread.
 
• Ecological Role: Often found in damp or marshy environments.
 
• Common Name: Known as horsetails or scouring rushes.

• Since molecules have more freedom of movement than in solids, **kinetic energy is higher than in solids but lower than in gases**.
 
 
 
• **Gaseous State (Maximum Kinetic Energy)**
 
 
• In gases, molecules are **widely spread out** with very weak intermolecular forces.
 
• They move randomly at high speeds in all directions.
 
• Since gas molecules are in constant motion with high velocity, **they possess the maximum kinetic energy**.

• Temperature decreases with height in this layer.

• The ionosphere is a part of this layer. It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is known as the ionosphere. 
 
• Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission.

questions.question: As a factor of cost, what is the other name of the net national product?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** National income**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National income__ is __equivalent__ to the __Net National Product__ at __factor cost__.

 __
 
• At factor costs, the Net National Product (NNP) equals the national revenue.
 
• The Gross National Product (GNP) of an economy is the GNP less the "depreciation" loss. It can be calculated using the following formula: NNP = GNP - Depreciation.
 
• National income is another name for Net National Product at Factor Cost. The sum of value added at factor cost, net domestic product at factor cost, and net factor income from overseas is known as the "Net National Product at Factor Cost."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The entire income of all country's citizens is referred to as the national income. As a result, it represents the nation's overall income.
 
• It is regarded as one of the most crucial characteristics for contrasting the growth of nations. A nation's economic activity determines its national income.
 
• By calculating the national income, the government may assess a nation's economic development, make plans for future growth, and establish its economic policy.
